rationale: I read the complete held EO 13422 (72 FR 2763, Jan. 18, 2007, 'Further Amendment to Executive Order 12866 on Regulatory Planning and Review'): it amends EO 12866 (policy statement and definitions of 'guidance document', significant guidance, regulatory plan and OIRA review; creation of Regulatory Policy Officers and their role); it is an amending order with no own term and no savings clause. I read the complete held EO 13497 (74 FR 6113, Jan. 30, 2009, 'Revocation of Certain Executive Orders Concerning Regulatory Planning and Review'): sec. 1 provides 'Executive Order 13258 of February 26, 2002, and Executive Order 13422 of January 18, 2007, concerning regulatory planning and review, which amended Executive Order 12866 of September 30, 1993, are revoked'; sec. 2 directs OMB and agencies to rescind implementing orders and guidance 'to the extent consistent with law'; sec. 3 is a no-private-right clause. The revocation names EO 13422 by number with no exception, delay or savings clause, so the whole order ended on Jan. 30, 2009 (the machine ACT scope 'partial' reflects that the sentence also names EO 13258, not any limit on 13422). D6 self-check, each later event: EO 13777 (2017) and EO 14215 (2025) amend or cite EO 12866 'as amended' but do not mention EO 13422 and do not restore its text (EO 14215 sec. 3(b) re-words the 'agency' definition of EO 12866); EO 14219 (Feb. 19, 2025, the catalog 'See' lead) uses the term 'guidance document' 'as defined in Executive Order 13422' in its own definitions, which borrows a definition by reference inside a new order and neither re-enacts nor revives EO 13422's commands; the held text of EO 14219 contains no other reference. I found no earlier own-term ending and no instrument between 2007 and 2009 amending EO 13422. Provisional NO hypothesis only.
